findings.reason: an arm that passes on unfixed code measures nothing, and the node would close on a gate that never failed.
findings.text: §9's first arm asserts that a first dispatch of a waiting node answers with phase `awaiting-upstream` and its waits, which the base revision already does (a) `test_a_queued_request_waits_on_its_dependencies.py::test_a_dispatch_holds_the_request_it_queues_for_upstream` asserts exactly that, and (b) the message the plan blames is produced only when a pointer already exists (`dispatch.py:404` `_answer_existing_node_run`, reached at `dispatch.py:1987` under `existing is not None`), so "routes the first dispatch through `_answer_existing_node_run`" is a control with nothing to disable

findings.reason: the repair would be aimed at a function the first dispatch never reaches — either the reported duplicate reading has a different cause (the coordinator's own second call, or the held `detail` wording) or the defect does not exist, and a node briefed on this mechanism would change `_answer_existing_node_run` and leave the observed wording untouched.
findings.text: the section says "The answer comes from `_answer_existing_node_run`, which a first dispatch reaches after its own `_queue_validated_waits` write", but the first-dispatch path (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1917` `_queue_validated_waits`, then `1921-1985` `if waiting: raise held` with `detail: "waiting on …"`) never reaches `dispatch.py:1987`, whose branch requires `existing is not None and (existing_phase == QUEUED_PHASE or is_local)`; the message the plan quotes therefore comes from a re-dispatch of a node whose pointer already exists, not from a first dispatch

findings.reason: s7 can be released as soon as s5 lands and would then implement a stall verdict that reads a duration field no landed section writes, which is exactly the "awaiting-upstream" wait the declaration exists to enforce.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` gives s7 only `#s5` and `a-review-gate-judges-what-it-covers#s10`, but §7 (`plan.html:122`) records "the stage that held it and that stage's last duration", and those per-stage durations and their verdict rows are introduced by §2 (release seconds) and §3 (`started_at`, `ended_at`, per-stage seconds, `plan.html:76`)

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `queue_admission.py`, `queue_landing.py`, `queue_edit.py`, `promotion`-family modules, `routing.py`, `plan_review.py`, `recovery_wait.py`, `runs.py`, `dispatch.py`, `fleet_supervisor.py` and `reckon/crew_run_commands.py` all resolve; `admit_once`, `admit_until_stopped`, `land_once`, `_land`, `resolve_waits`, `require_plan_reviewed`, `review_coverage`, `move_queued_run`, `_answer_existing_node_run`, `_queue_validated_waits`, `CompetenceLimit`, `held-on-claim` and `held-until-changed` all exist; the extensionless cross-plan hrefs `/reckon/plans/a-queue-holds-the-whole-plan#s18|#s29|#s32` and `a-review-gate-judges-what-it-covers#s10` resolve as `<path>.html` with `id` anchors present.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §9's first arm (`plan.html:147`) and its negative control cannot disagree, because a first dispatch already answers with phase `awaiting-upstream` from the lane-held branch in `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1921-1985`, which runs before the branch that control would re-route (`dispatch.py:1987`).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate writes a new file under `tests/`; §4's timing arm logs under the run's `logs/` inside the durable run directory, not a node-local temporary path, and the plan's own measurements cite `~/.config/reckon/crew/admission-verdicts.jsonl`, which exists.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the one new symbol named (`queue_admission.release_waiters`) and every new test file name describe the mechanism, and no section, comment or symbol carries a plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §9's stated root cause (a first dispatch is answered by `_answer_existing_node_run`) is contradicted by the caller chain it cites (`dispatch.py:1917` → `_queue_validated_waits` → `dispatch.py:1921-1985` raises `LaneHeld` with `detail: "waiting on …"` before `dispatch.py:1987`, whose guard requires `existing is not None`).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of §2–§9 names one deliverable (a numbered list of arms measuring that one change); §4's timing arm and §2's live-interval recording measure the same change rather than a second one.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §7 (`plan.html:122`) names the stall verdict by "the stage that held it and that stage's last duration", and per-stage durations are written only by §3's landing/admission loops, yet `plan-section-depends-on` (`plan.html:22`) gives s7 only `work-is-never-stuck-behind-the-admission-loop#s5` and `a-review-gate-judges-what-it-covers#s10`.
